principles.instruction: Annotate only the FINDINGS and IMPRESSION sections of the radiology report. Do not annotate the IMAGE, INDICATION, or COMPARISON sections.
principles.applies_when: The report has structured sections with headers such as IMAGE, INDICATION, COMPARISON, FINDINGS, IMPRESSION.
exceptions: If section headers are absent, annotate the narrative clinical description and final conclusion/impression portions.

principles.instruction: Split text into minimal contiguous spans that represent either an anatomical entity or an observation/descriptor. Label each span with exactly one of {ANAT, OBS-DP, OBS-DA, OBS-U}. Do not annotate punctuation or pure function/cue words (e.g., 'no', 'without', 'may', 'negative', 'for') unless they are part of a compound term (e.g., 'noncalcified'). Annotate every relevant token/span in the FINDINGS and IMPRESSION sections.
principles.applies_when: Always, for every token or phrase in the annotation scope.

principles.instruction: Label as ANAT: body parts, organs, anatomical regions, laterality/direction modifiers, anatomical adjectives (e.g., pleural, pulmonary, cardiac, mediastinal, hilar, interstitial, bronchovascular, diaphragmatic, bony, vascular, humeral, thoracic, retrocardiac), and anatomical descriptors used to specify or locate a structure (e.g., contour, silhouette, size, spine, rib, atrium, quadrant, interspace, lobe, hilum, aorta). Multiword anatomical phrases are annotated component by component. Laterality/direction words (right, left, upper, lower, posterior, anterior, distal, superior, lateral) are ANAT when they modify an anatomical structure; if they modify a finding or procedure, follow the observation rules.
principles.applies_when: A span denotes anatomy, location, or an anatomical attribute, even when embedded in a finding phrase.
exceptions: Words that are primarily disease/finding names (e.g., cardiomegaly, effusion, pneumothorax, hernia, pneumonia, opacity, nodule, mass) are observations, not ANAT, even if they contain anatomical roots.
